questions.question: div vs section vs article — what is the deciding factor?
questions.answer: Meaning. div is a generic container with no semantics. section is a named thematic part of the page, usually with a heading. article is self-contained and could be syndicated on its own.

questions.question: When do you use strong/em instead of b/i?
questions.answer: strong and em carry meaning (importance, stress emphasis) that assistive tech can convey. b and i apply visual bold/italic with no semantic weight, for brand names or alternate tone.

questions.question: Why can duplicate ids break a page even if it looks fine?
questions.answer: Fragment links jump to the first match, label for and aria-labelledby resolve unpredictably, and getElementById returns one element. The page renders but interactions and accessibility break.

questions.question: Can title replace alt on an image?
questions.answer: No. alt provides the accessible name and is required; title is advisory tooltip text, unreliable on touch and inconsistently announced. Use alt for meaning and title only as an optional hint.

questions.question: Does POST make a login form secure?
questions.answer: No. POST moves data from the URL to the body but does not encrypt it. HTTPS is required, and credentials must be handled securely on the server.

questions.question: label for=email but the input has name=email and no id. What happens?
questions.answer: The label is not associated with the input: clicking it does nothing and the accessible name is missing. for must match an id.

questions.question: Name the void elements and explain what makes an attribute boolean.
questions.answer: Void elements include img, br, hr, input, meta, link, source, track, wbr, area, base, col, embed, param. Boolean attributes are true when present regardless of value: required, disabled, checked, hidden, readonly, autofocus.

questions.question: Why is a table a bad layout tool, and what does a missing doctype change?
questions.answer: Tables encode data relationships; using them for layout confuses screen readers and fights responsive design — use CSS grid/flexbox. A missing doctype triggers quirks mode with legacy box sizing and layout behavior.
